- Model consistently underestimates prices in early days of the 30-day forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–7 days.
- Overshoots occur after sharp upward spikes in the history (e.g., 90.01 → 84.76), leading to overprediction of subsequent values.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: forecasts tend to revert to lower levels after recent high prices, but often overshoots the true mean.
- Forecasts lag behind true values by 1–3 days in the early part of the horizon, especially when true values show upward momentum.
- Model overreacts to recent low prices, predicting a sharper rebound than observed (e.g., 80.88 → 84.76 vs. 81.30 → 82.76).
- Forecasts are overly sensitive to the most recent 3–5 data points, leading to overfitting to short-term volatility.
- Model underestimates the persistence of recent trends, especially when true values show sustained upward momentum.
- Forecasts tend to be too conservative in the final 5–7 days of the horizon, missing late-stage upward or downward corrections.
- Model fails to capture the “tail” of the distribution — often underestimates the magnitude of late-stage corrections or spikes.
- Forecasts show a tendency to “smooth” out volatility, underestimating sudden drops or spikes in the true outcome.
